slides.0.title: McLaren Vale and Adelaide Hills
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 3 · Lesson 2
slides.1.title: McLaren Vale: Mediterranean Meets the Sea
slides.1.points.0: Location: 35 km south of Adelaide; cooled by Gulf St Vincent sea breezes
slides.1.points.1: Soil: incredibly diverse — over 40 distinct soil types in a small area
slides.1.points.2: Climate: Mediterranean; warm days, cool nights thanks to ocean influence
slides.1.points.3: Key varieties: Shiraz, Grenache, Mourvèdre (GSM) + Cabernet, Fiano, Nero d'Avola
slides.1.points.4: Style: rich, supple reds with dark fruit, chocolate and olive/savoury notes
slides.2.title: Adelaide Hills: SA's Cool-Climate Gem
slides.2.points.0: Location: in the Mount Lofty Ranges, 15–45 km east of Adelaide; altitude 400–710 m
slides.2.points.1: Climate: cool; rainfall higher than rest of SA — average 20°C in ripening season
slides.2.points.2: Key varieties: Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Syrah (cooler expressions)
slides.2.points.3: Style: elegant, high-acid whites; florally expressive, lean reds
slides.2.points.4: Notable: Shaw + Smith, Henschke, Ashton Hills lead quality

slides.4.question: Why is McLaren Vale particularly suited to Grenache-Shiraz-Mourvèdre (GSM) blends?
slides.4.options.0: Because it is the coldest region in Australia
slides.4.options.1: The warm Mediterranean climate and maritime cooling create full-bodied, spicy reds with excellent ripeness — ideal for these southern French varieties
slides.4.options.2: Because government regulations require GSM production there
slides.4.options.3: The soil is identical to Châteauneuf-du-Pape
slides.4.explanation: McLaren Vale's warm Mediterranean climate ensures full phenolic ripeness for Grenache, Shiraz and Mourvèdre, while the cooling Gulf St Vincent sea breezes preserve freshness and spice. The resulting GSM blends are rich yet fragrant — mirroring the style of southern Rhône wines but with an unmistakably Australian character.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: McLaren Vale: warm Mediterranean + 40+ soil types → rich Shiraz and GSM blends
slides.5.points.1: Adelaide Hills: high altitude (400–710 m) cool-climate → elegant whites (Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay)
slides.5.points.2: These two neighbouring regions illustrate SA's remarkable diversity
